candidateOwnership.direction: Economic policy, responsible business and sustainability

interestReview.finding: All 41 own rows were read and reconciled against the current target. Same substantive direction structure as English sibling is independently supported by the Dutch page and OER; English sibling IDs are not imported.

academicJudgment.positive: Sustained micro/macro/public/behavioural economics and econometrics, accounting, banking and firm study directly address this Dutch target’s confirmed academic core. The environmental, political and social courses supply specific policy/responsible-firm complements. Both actual options preserve six taught economics courses.
academicJudgment.limits: Dedicated development/labour/game-theory/economic-history sequences, deeper accounting/corporate finance, a second econometrics stage and required economics thesis are not reproduced. Language identity alone creates neither positive equivalence nor negative proof.
academicJudgment.adverseTest: If old-method preparation or another sequence is required for the thesis, eligibility changes but the confirmed taught core and narrower UCR response remain. If the new courses satisfy the names, the response likewise remains. No formal answer is assumed.

courseReview.reuseBoundary: Same actual 29 course facts, all 48 placements and specific concept roles as independently checked CP041. Course evidence and selected descriptions are unchanged by exact code/version; reuse is justified by the direct official same-content statement and separate Dutch academic-core check, not by CP041 approval. All contributions are tested against CP042’s own core/candidate map.

candidateReview.substantiveDifference: The second option replaces specialist banking, mathematical statistics, marketing and organizational study with international politics, planetary foundations, sociology, environmental justice and commercial law; core economics remains.

rejected.label: Finance and financial market stability
rejected.reason: Money, Banking & Finance supplies asset pricing, risk, regulation and a bank simulation; Accounting adds investment appraisal. Both are already in the closest programme. These real contributions do not supply a sustained distinct 24-course finance route with further specialist investment and risk study.

rejected.label: Accounting and financial reporting
rejected.reason: The current UCR workbook has one accounting and corporate finance course but no advanced financial reporting, management accounting, auditing or control sequence to anchor a separate 24-course accounting route.

stopping.assessment: The closest UCR response retains economic theory, finance, business and quantitative research. The second route shifts five substantive courses toward economic policy, responsible firms and sustainability. Both remain feasible and differ by five courses each. Separate specialist finance and accounting routes are evidenced but cannot form credible distinct 24-course programmes from the current UCR offer without weak substitutes.

alignmentReview.finding: Each component was checked against the same primary subject/method relationship using CP042’s actual translated component names. No language-based equivalence is asserted. One econometrics course appears once; banking is not silently assigned to corporate finance/financial policy. Approved choice and thesis retain their distinct roles. Optional UCR research is additional to 180 EC.

sourceFirstChallenge.reviewerOrPass: CP042 separately identified same-AI source-first second pass
sourceFirstChallenge.method: Re-established the Dutch identity and first-year table from the current official Dutch page and actual OER pp.34/36/39 before challenging the finished decision/canonical pair against current UCR content. No independent human or separate-agent review.
sourceFirstChallenge.challenge: The Dutch target could have had a different route or syllabus, making English-sibling reuse invalid. The actual main page explicitly states shared academic content and separates first-year teaching language; the adopted bilingual table confirms the distinct Dutch courses and common policy route. Thus reuse is bounded to actual content, not registry identity or approval.
sourceFirstChallenge.academicChallenge: A general environmental/social programme with an economics label would fail. Both actual options instead retain six taught economics courses including empirical econometrics, concrete accounting and firm study. The second reallocates five courses around independently evidenced responsibility/policy questions. Dedicated disciplinary gaps remain unmatched; coherence alone does not confer comparability.
sourceFirstChallenge.adverseResolution: An extra old-method requirement, changed preparation or sequencing may affect thesis access. The narrower claim concerns independently confirmed subjects and the actual UCR response; neither outcome removes that core. No equivalence or waiver is certified.
sourceFirstChallenge.candidateChallenge: Specialist finance and accounting leads were retested from their real taught positive content, including asset pricing, instruments, risk, bank simulation and investment appraisal. These contributions already occur in the closest option and do not establish a sustained distinct further specialist curriculum.
sourceFirstChallenge.otherFormalFacts: Article 16 links the mandatory academic-language test to a first-year component; Appendix 6 states 42 EC for full-time first-year advice. Article 17 retains non-overlap/approval and master/HBO limits. These reader notes are retained from supported own prior research, without extra credits.

contentReview.finding: The English display title and translated first-year labels are retained from the latest CP042 canonical. The Dutch first-year identity and exact 2025-entry cohort are explicit. Documented 180 EC is not formal pathway certification. Approved 24-EC choice is not unknown study. Specialist gaps, thesis-entry uncertainty and unscheduled optional research are visible and proportionate. No internal source logs are selected.
contentReview.descriptionReuse: All 29 exact-code description texts and source/workbook versions are identical to the read and hash-verified CP041 entries. Their actual relevance was separately assessed against CP042’s core; no cache bytes changed.
contentReview.runtime: CP042 itself is not browser-tested. Unchanged renderer and the identical qualified-180-EC presentation mode were actually tested on CP041 at e3594b0ed7e487be925062c9e3b4309605323b4f with ordinary/unresolved controls; no new presentation type is introduced.
